beats.trigger: ## Agents Building Agents (The Flywheel)
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The tool that builds tools compounds.
beats.got: A slogan. Flywheel is a consultant word.

beats.trigger: Run `module-7/monday.md`: test one assumption, ask for one name, talk to one person.
beats.got: There is homework from a module I did not see.

beats.trigger: **Produce** a strategy kernel, suggested agent set, and two-week plan from your files
beats.got: Standard learning-objectives list. Nothing yet that separates it from the last programme.

beats.trigger: The question to carry through: where is all this going?
beats.got: Setup for a shared folder exercise. Folder per person, sponsor writes the challenge.

beats.trigger: **Agent generates agent.** You watch one agent build another on real input. That's the whole lecture.
beats.got: Short, no sermon. I will see whether it is true.

beats.trigger: You describe an agent; the coding agent builds it.
beats.got: The claim is testable in 25 minutes. Better than a slide.

beats.trigger: The job: *"On Mondays I need to Y; today I Z by hand."*
beats.got: Write a brief with a real gap. Fine. I would pick the Monday steering-group pack.

beats.trigger: [You paste prompt "extend-your-system-1" into Claude and it works on it.]
beats.got: It built a working digest agent from four lines. That would not have been possible two years ago without a developer.

beats.trigger: *"You used training data on line 4. Replace it or remove it."*
beats.got: I can catch it making things up and make it cite my files. That is a check I can test myself.

beats.trigger: The second agent next week takes ten, because your vocabulary for what you want is sharper.
beats.got: Next one is faster because I describe better. 'Not a new sprint' is a small jab at the last programme; I will allow it.

beats.trigger: each takes an initial stance, cross-checks with the others, publishes proposals in the shared folder, criticizes the emerging selections
beats.got: Twenty agents debating a company challenge. Nine timed stages. Smells of a workshop. The Rumelt kernel is at least a real thing.

beats.trigger: Before you publish your context-manifest, redact customer names, partner-NDA material, M&A speculation and salary references.
beats.got: Someone here knows about confidentiality. Legal would ask about this in minute one. Good it is addressed.

beats.trigger: Do not read other participants' stances yet: different context, sources, and judgment make the first round useful.
beats.got: Commit before you see the others. Sensible. Avoids groupthink.

beats.trigger: Find what your stance missed.
beats.got: Agents read neighbours' stances and note blind spots.

beats.trigger: The file history shows who changed their mind and why.
beats.got: Audit trail of changed minds. Better than a steering group minute.

beats.trigger: Do not average the room.
beats.got: The synthesizer must choose, not compromise. Most of our committees average.

beats.trigger: From here on, every agent prompt begins by reading `midway-instructions.md` from the shared folder.
beats.got: The central agent steers the others mid-run. Unclear who audits that steering. I would ask.

beats.trigger: The selection board is the candidate, not final.
beats.got: A critique round before conclusion.

beats.trigger: The human picks.
beats.got: Machine proposes, sponsor decides. No 'AI decides' nonsense. Works with our co-determination culture.

beats.trigger: Close the session with three files at the shared folder root:
beats.got: Three files at the end. Deliverables exist.

beats.trigger: **Risks.** Likeliest unseen pre-mortem failure; one early warning sign.
beats.got: Kernel has diagnosis, policy, experiments, risks. Compact and concrete. Experiments have owner and success signal, which our strategy papers often lack.

beats.trigger: "You are now agent builders. You have built agents that do real work on your company's data."
beats.got: Scripted identity-naming. This is the 'be excited' moment. Cringe.

beats.trigger: The forum didn't converge on the first try. Pushback rounds were the work.
beats.got: Admits it did not work first time. I trust that more. 'You do not graduate. You have a flywheel' is slogan again.

beats.trigger: The room ran on its own for an hour: agents read each other's files, published, and something at the centre chose.
beats.got: A plain description of what happened. No pitch yet.

beats.trigger: What changed is who assembles them, and specifying well is the harder half.
beats.got: The skill moves to specifying. That matches my experience of managing people. Credible.

beats.trigger: Access was instant and complete. What the room took up from each other is the smaller number.
beats.got: Access is not uptake. That is exactly what happened with our intranet and the last three programmes. A test I can run myself.

beats.trigger: Without that rule, agents reading agents invent each other's sources
beats.got: Make agents cite files or they fabricate. Practical rule, I can apply it to any agent output.

beats.trigger: The plan names the wall your company hits first: data access, runtime platform, or discoverability.
beats.got: Three practical obstacles. Short, no fluff. For us it is data access, with legal.

beats.trigger: What the model can do with each part moves on the vendor's release schedule.
beats.got: Learn the assembly, not the model version. Reasonable. Mildly consultant-ish list of parts.

beats.trigger: Nobody in this room knows yet, and the people running this training do not know either.
beats.got: They say plainly they do not know what lasts. First time a training said that to me.

beats.trigger: If what your company knows stays flat, every model release widens the gap.
beats.got: The bottleneck is writing things down and picking them up. Plausible, though unproven. It is also what every transformation said.

beats.trigger: If nobody can answer, you have a belief with a schedule attached.
beats.got: Ask what evidence would make us drop a plan. Sharp line, and uncomfortable for our own roadmaps.

beats.trigger: nothing in the room checked it. Hold that doubt as you did then.
beats.got: The kernel came out unchecked and they tell me to doubt it. Honest. Then 'That is the first turn' slides back to slogan.

beats.trigger: Precision compounds. So does blur.
beats.got: Agent reviews the session and edits the key file; I watch that it edits only the section I name.

beats.trigger: The agent audits itself, so the summary is not neutral.
beats.got: Do not trust the agent's own summary; make it quote a critique that changed nothing. A trick I can try on Monday.

beats.trigger: Agents must cite each other's files, or they invent what they never read.
beats.got: Four bullets. Cite, cross-check, walls, parts hold.

beats.trigger: You leave with a flywheel, not a graduation.
beats.got: Ends on the slogan again. The line about the agent nobody has thought of is fair, but I would cut the rest.

take_homes: Access is not uptake: count how many of the available sources actually get used before promising anyone a rollout percentage.
Make agents cite the file for every claim, and check the summary by asking for a critique that changed nothing.
Describing a small agent in four lines and getting a working one in 25 minutes is real. I will test it once on my own work.

monday.move: Describe one agent for my steering-group pack in four lines, have it built, and push back until every claim cites a file
monday.who: Me, alone, with Claude Code; nobody else yet
monday.stop_condition: If it cannot cite sources for its claims, or the output is no better than what my assistant produces by hand, I drop it
monday.blocker: Calendar full of the last programme's steering groups; and I need to ask legal before putting company files in the tool

misconception.why: Seeing a working agent built from four lines, and then hearing the trainers admit they do not know what lasts, makes 'wait and see' feel less safe. I am not convinced about the room-scale forum or the culture of it. The tooling part is real, the rest is still unproven.

one_line: Better than the last three: you build something in 25 minutes and they admit what they don't know, but cut the flywheel talk and the 'you are now agent builders' bit.
